Uh we're bringing a special show this week.
We have been running a series of shows that we recorded at the Center for the Holographic Arts in Long Island City, New York.
But we had some news come through that we've been waiting for for quite some time.
And I'd like to uh at least dedicate this program to that news.
Our special guest this week is going to be Franz Ross from Ross Books, and I'm joined right now with Michelle Roy once again in the studio.
Michelle, how are you doing?
I'm good, how are you?
Okay, because you're involved with this project to some extent as well.
Uh to quite a big extent in some areas that we'll get into in just a second.

Uh but what's happened is over the past year, or maybe a little bit more than a year, we've been work working with Ross Books, who has published the holography handbook and holography marketplace, to publish shoebox holography as a regular book.
As many of you know that shoebox holography was designed around the semiconductor lasers and a little system that students are using and even some amateurs and hobbyists uh to create holograms.

Franz Ross gave me a call and said they were interested in doing the book a little over a year ago, and since that time we've been working on it and now it's going to be released on April 14th and will be available in bookstores across the country and also your regular internet outlets such as Amazon.com, Barnes and Nobles, etc.
Michelle's involved with this to the point that you did a appendix to the book as far as uh career development with students.

And along that vein, what I'd like to do having you on uh the show right now is uh to get a f a few of your thoughts on how you feel that shoebox holography ties into the educational curriculum of a lot of the schools.

I think that one of the trends that we see in schools is that they're moving to more project oriented curricula where kids are rather than sitting and reading a book about lasers or holography or whatever, not that they don't need to read books, um, but actually having hands on experiences, particularly in the sciences, is incredibly important in terms of helping kids understand the underlying, you know, scientific principles and how everything works.

And I think the the great thing about the shoebox book is that it shows teachers and students, you know, step by step how to go through a project of creating a hologram that gives kids a real hands on experience with the technology and the scientific principles.

Plus the fact that a lot of schools are going to more interdisciplinary approaches where they're um having, you know, it's not just uh you know one subject on its own and there's so many, you know, math, physics, you know, all of those things tie into what you do with shoebox.
So, you know, that's a real opportunity for for teachers to do something that's not only project oriented um and hands on, but also uh interdisciplinary.
So it was the shoebox holography guide that allowed holography itself to become part of the uh state standards in Florida with communication technologies.
And the way that Bill Pugh and I worked on that was showing it was very important that we showed how other areas of education can tie in with the hit on uh different standards.
Um and mo and most states are moving to standards based education.

So if schools are looking for a way to you know have a unit, you know, in a science class or whatever that hits across multiple standards because many schools are complaining, well how the heck are we supposed to cover all of this, you know, in in a school year or over the course of a kid's um life in the schools, well this is something that hits across multiple standards and so those would you know be satisfied in one project.
Yeah.

Um so and by the end of this school year, I will have a program guide together for teachers w which will show them how they can bring a number of different students with different interests into this whole process and all center around the science and technology of shoe box holography.

Well, and you could even have teachers working together to on the you know you can have the teachers that have who have the same kids in the science class, you know, and and they work together so that it's actually the same kids.
Yeah.
Just in their different classes.
So we'll get that program to guide together for teachers as well, and you uh would be able to order that along with the shoebox holography uh book itself.
Also another area of the book that you wrote yourself.
The careers, right?
Careers and lasers.
Yeah, and you want to tell the uh little bit about it.

Yeah, I mean, very quickly, um one of the things that we wanted to do was um not was also look at how you know if kids found that they were interested or anyone found that they were interested in the whole uh field of lasers and photonics as a result of going through the shoebox holography, they could then explore uh different career options.
So that the appendix that I wrote basically talks about what are the different aspects that you have to consider in career development.
We did a show, you know, earlier in the season talking about that.

So that's all in that appendix so that if kids or whoever are interested in getting into a career, they could, you know, do some more exploration.
